duties: Heads the government and runs all executive departments, bureaus and offices
Commander-in-chief of the Armed Forces
Appoints Cabinet secretaries, ambassadors and senior military officers (many need Commission on Appointments consent), and judges from Judicial and Bar Council lists
Proposes the national budget to Congress each year and can veto bills or budget items
Negotiates treaties (the Senate must approve them) and leads foreign policy
Grants pardons and, with Congress, amnesty
Delivers the State of the Nation Address
not: Cannot pass laws alone: Congress makes laws
Cannot spend money Congress has not approved in the budget
quals: Natural-born citizen
Registered voter, able to read and write
At least 40 years old on election day
Lived in the Philippines for 10 years before the election
ask: What will they prioritise in the national budget, and how will it be paid for?
Who would they appoint to run key departments?
What did they do in past executive or management posts?

jobs.term: 6 years, at most 2 terms in a row
jobs.pick: Vote for 1 (elected separately from the President)
duties: Takes over if the President dies, is removed, resigns or is permanently disabled
May be appointed to the Cabinet by the President (no confirmation needed)
Runs the Office of the Vice President and the programmes Congress funds in its budget
not: The Constitution gives the VP no other fixed powers: most of the job depends on what the President assigns
quals: Same as President: natural-born citizen, registered voter, able to read and write
At least 40 years old on election day
Lived in the Philippines for 10 years before the election
ask: Are they ready to take over as President if needed?
What would they do with the Office of the Vice President's budget?

jobs.term: 6 years, at most 2 terms in a row
duties: Writes, debates and votes on national laws
Reviews and approves the national budget with the House
Approves or rejects treaties (two-thirds of senators must agree)
Acts as judge in impeachment trials
Holds hearings (inquiries in aid of legislation) to look into issues and problems in government
Some senators sit on the Commission on Appointments, which confirms Cabinet members and other officials
not: Does not build roads or hand out aid: government agencies carry out projects. Since 2013 the Supreme Court has barred legislators from choosing or releasing project funds after the budget is passed
quals: Natural-born citizen
At least 35 years old on election day
Registered voter, able to read and write
Lived in the Philippines for 2 years before the election
ask: What laws have they written or pushed, and what happened to them?
How did they vote on major bills or on the budget?
Which committee work or hearings have they led?

jobs.term: 3 years, at most 3 terms in a row
duties: Writes and votes on national laws, including bills for their district
Budget, tax and tariff bills must start in the House
Only the House can start an impeachment case
Represents the district's needs in Congress
not: Does not carry out projects or release funds: agencies and local governments do. The Supreme Court barred legislators from choosing or releasing project funds after the budget is passed (2013)
quals: Natural-born citizen
At least 25 years old on election day
Registered voter in the district, able to read and write
Lived in the district for at least 1 year before the election
ask: Which bills have they filed or passed, and did they help the district?
Do they show up for sessions and votes?

jobs.term: 3 years, at most 3 terms in a row
jobs.pick: Vote for 1 party, not a person
duties: Party-list groups win House seats according to their share of the national party-list vote
Their nominees serve as House members, with the same law-making work as district representatives
Meant to give a voice to sectors and groups that may not win district seats
not: You vote for the group, and the group's list decides who sits in the House: check who its nominees are
quals: Nominees: natural-born citizen, registered voter, able to read and write
At least 25 years old on election day (youth-sector nominees: 25 to 30)
Bona fide member of the party for at least 90 days before the election
Lived in the Philippines for at least 1 year before the election
ask: Who are the group's nominees, and what is their connection to the sector?
What has the group done in the House?

jobs.term: 3 years, at most 3 terms in a row
duties: Chief executive of the province: carries out provincial laws (ordinances) and programmes
Prepares the provincial budget and can veto ordinances
Appoints provincial officials and employees
Runs services handed to provinces, such as provincial hospitals, agricultural support and roads linking towns
not: Does not run towns and cities: their mayors do
quals: Filipino citizen, registered voter in the area, resident there at least 1 year before election day, able to read and write Filipino or a local language
At least 23 years old on election day
ask: How has the provincial budget been spent, and on what?
What is their plan for provincial hospitals, farm support and roads?

jobs.term: 3 years, at most 3 terms in a row
duties: Presides over the provincial board (Sangguniang Panlalawigan) and votes only to break a tie
Approves the board's own spending
Takes over as Governor if the post becomes vacant
quals: Filipino citizen, registered voter in the area, resident there at least 1 year before election day, able to read and write Filipino or a local language
At least 23 years old on election day
ask: How do they run board sessions, and what ordinances have they moved?

jobs.term: 3 years, at most 3 terms in a row
jobs.pick: Vote for the number shown on your ballot
duties: Passes provincial ordinances and resolutions
Approves the provincial budget
Sets provincial taxes, fees and charges within the limits of law
quals: Filipino citizen, registered voter in the area, resident there at least 1 year before election day, able to read and write Filipino or a local language
At least 23 years old on election day
ask: Which ordinances have they written, and how did they vote on the budget?

jobs.term: 3 years, at most 3 terms in a row
duties: Chief executive of the city or town: carries out ordinances and runs local offices
Prepares the local budget and can veto ordinances
Appoints city or municipal officials and employees
Oversees local police operations and leads disaster response
Issues business permits and licences
Runs basic services such as health centres, garbage collection, public markets and day care
quals: Filipino citizen, registered voter in the area, resident there at least 1 year before election day, able to read and write Filipino or a local language
At least 21 years old on election day (23 in highly urbanized cities)
ask: How has the city or town budget been spent?
What is their plan for health, garbage, traffic or flooding?
How do they handle permits and disaster response?

jobs.term: 3 years, at most 3 terms in a row
duties: Presides over the city or municipal council (Sangguniang Panlungsod or Bayan) and votes only to break a tie
Approves the council's own spending
Takes over as Mayor if the post becomes vacant
quals: Filipino citizen, registered voter in the area, resident there at least 1 year before election day, able to read and write Filipino or a local language
At least 21 years old on election day (23 in highly urbanized cities)
ask: How do they run council sessions, and what ordinances have they moved?

jobs.term: 3 years, at most 3 terms in a row
jobs.pick: Vote for the number shown on your ballot
duties: Passes city or municipal ordinances and resolutions
Approves the local budget
Sets local taxes, fees and charges within the limits of law
Approves zoning and land-use plans and franchises such as for tricycles
quals: Filipino citizen, registered voter in the area, resident there at least 1 year before election day, able to read and write Filipino or a local language
At least 18 years old on election day (23 in highly urbanized cities)
ask: Which ordinances have they written, and do they attend sessions?
